title: When the Water Rises and Your Wheelchair Doesn't Fit in the Truck

body.en: A flood evacuation is underway. You use a wheelchair that's essential to your daily independence, and the rescue vehicle arriving has no ramp and limited space. What should you insist on, right now?

choices.label: Tell the rescue team clearly that your wheelchair is essential equipment, not luggage, and ask what accessible transport options exist
choices.consequence: Right approach. Assistive devices aren't optional extras — leaving one behind can mean someone can't move safely for weeks afterward. Naming the need clearly is how it gets addressed instead of overlooked in the rush.

choices.label: Leave the wheelchair behind to make space and worry about it later
choices.consequence: This creates a second emergency. Without the wheelchair, independent movement afterward — getting food, reaching medical care, using a shelter — becomes far harder, right when everything else is already disrupted.

choices.label: Say nothing and hope someone thinks of it
choices.consequence: Too risky. In a fast-moving evacuation, needs that aren't clearly stated are the ones most likely to get missed entirely.
